title: A closed subscheme whose fibres are Cartier divisors is locally contained in a relative effective Cartier divisor, and agrees with one under flatness or local principality

standard_prerequisites.name: Relative effective Cartier divisors and their stability under base change, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the construction performed on an approximating Noetherian model back to the original situation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Approximation of a flat and finitely presented algebra by a flat finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring, Grothendieck's generic freeness and nonzerodivisor statement, the existence of a neighbourhood on which a regular element stays regular with flat quotient, and the openness of flatness, all cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: These four inputs produce the element g outside the prime about which the constructed divisor is a relative effective Cartier divisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjective map of flat local algebras essentially of finite presentation that becomes an isomorphism after dividing by the maximal ideal is an isomorphism, and the local criterion for an isomorphism in a neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the containment of part (1) to an equality under the flatness hypothesis of part (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: The equivalence between the source morphism of a closed subscheme being locally of finite presentation and the composite being so, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Deduces the final statements of the lemma from parts (2) and (3).

core_obligations: Set up the local situation: choose affine neighbourhoods of the point of the source and its image, let the ideal of the closed subscheme be I, and use the hypothesis of (1) to shrink until the image of I in the fibre over the given base point is generated by a single nonzerodivisor; choose an element f of I mapping to that generator and claim that, after inverting some element outside the prime, the vanishing locus of f is a relative effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 4215-4232).

Approximate by a Noetherian model: using the flat finite presentation approximation, spread the situation out to a flat finite type map of Noetherian rings with an element f_0 whose specialization is f, observe that f_0 is a nonzerodivisor in the corresponding fibre, apply Grothendieck's statement to get that f_0 is a nonzerodivisor at the relevant prime with flat quotient, and then use the neighbourhood statement for regular elements together with the openness of flatness to find an element outside the prime over which both properties hold, so that the vanishing locus of f_0 is a relative effective Cartier divisor on the model; base change gives the claim (proof lines 4234-4262).

Prove part (2): with the divisor D of part (1) containing Z, consider the closed immersion of Z into D; the induced surjection of local rings is a map of flat local algebras essentially of finite presentation which becomes an isomorphism after dividing by the maximal ideal of the base, so it is an isomorphism, and hence the immersion is an isomorphism near the point by the local criterion (proof lines 4264-4274).

Prove part (3): shrink so that the ideals of D and of Z are each generated by a single element; their generators differ by a factor which is a unit on the fibre at the point because the two cut out the same effective Cartier divisor there, so that factor is a unit in the local ring and hence on a neighbourhood, showing that Z and D agree there (proof lines 4276-4284).

Deduce the final statements: if the closed subscheme is flat and locally of finite presentation over the base with all fibres effective Cartier divisors, part (2) applies to give equality with a relative effective Cartier divisor, and if it is locally principal with the same fibre condition then part (3) does; the hypothesis comparison uses the equivalence between finite presentation over the base and over the ambient scheme (proof lines 4286-4291).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to algebra and construct, after shrinking, a relative effective Cartier divisor containing the subscheme and agreeing with it on the fibre, using the Noetherian approximation and the openness of flatness (proof lines 4215-4262).
Upgrade the containment to equality in the two cases by an isomorphism criterion for flat local algebras and by comparing local equations, then deduce the final statements (proof lines 4264-4291).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a flat morphism locally of finite presentation a closed subscheme whose fibre at a point is a Cartier divisor is locally contained in a relative effective Cartier divisor agreeing with it on that fibre, with equality under a flatness or a local principality hypothesis, and it derives the corresponding global criteria (statement lines 4190-4213). The counted proof is a substantial local argument with genuinely different layers: it reduces to affine rings and to a single local equation on the fibre, spreads the situation out to a Noetherian model by the flat finite presentation approximation, uses Grothendieck's statement and the neighbourhood theorem for regular elements together with the openness of flatness to make the model's equation a relative effective Cartier divisor, base changes back, and then upgrades containment to equality by the isomorphism criterion for flat local algebras and by comparing local equations, finally deducing the global criteria (proof lines 4215-4291). It is H2: the argument is fully carried out in the counted span and its inputs are standard algebra theorems of the openness and approximation type.
